 Recap and reaction as Norris takes pole in wet Sao Paulo qualifying
 7 November 2026 Live Reporting (active) 
 Leaderboard 
 Summary
 Lando Norris takes pole in wet Sao Paulo Grand Prix qualifying
 Antonelli to start second, Lawson third and Hulkenberg fourth
 Alonso to start eighth after reaching Q3 for first time this season
 Heavy rain started just before session began, leading to delay of more than 80 minutes
 Hamilton and Verstappen to start from back of grid 
 Russell and Leclerc also have grid penalties
 Interlagos to stay on F1 calendar until 2035
 Select 'listen live' for BBC Radio 5 Sports Extra commentary (UK only)
 Close form Send us your F1 views
 Get involved Live Reporting
 Lorraine McKenna and Tasnim Chowdhury
 Report: Norris takes pole in rain-delayed qualifying published at 21:02 GMT 21:02 GMT 
 Andrew Benson 
BBC F1 correspondent 
 Image source, Getty Images McLaren's Lando Norris took pole position for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix in a wet qualifying session at Interlagos delayed by nearly an hour and a half for heavy rain. 
 Norris beat fellow Briton George Russell by 0.204 seconds, and the Mercedes driver was fuming that he could have been faster had he not been told by his engineer to abort a faster lap before the rain became heavier.
 In any case, Russell has a five-place grid penalty for exceeding his permitted number of engine parts, promoting team-mate and new world champion Kimi Antonelli to second.
 Ferrari's Charles Leclerc qualified fourth but has a 10-place grid penalty which promotes Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson to third.
 The New Zealander was one of a number of drivers to have their best qualifying session of the year thanks to the levelling effect of the wet weather.
 Also among them were Audi's Nico Hulkenberg, who qualified sixth and will start fourth, Haas driver Oliver Bearman, who was eighth and will start sixth, and Aston Martin's Fernando Alonso, who was ninth and will move up one place to eighth, plus Wlliams' Alex Albon, who is right behind Alonso.
 Read the full report here 
 16 2 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Sao Paulo GP build-up from 16:00 GMT on Sunday published at 21:00 GMT 21:00 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images Lando Norris had to pass on the championship crown last weekend to Kimi Antonelli in Mexico, but the McLaren driver is at least back in the number one spot after sealing his third pole position in Brazil in the wet conditions. 
 The McLaren driver has the new title holder alongside him on the front row with all the various grid penalties, so who will come out on top in Interlagos? 
 And more importantly, will the rain stay away? 
 That was a long old qualifying session tonight, and there is more rain forecast for Sunday's 71-lap grand prix. That could give the likes of Liam Lawson in P3 and Nico Hulkenberg in P4 the chance to score some excellent points this weekend. 
 But keep an eye out for Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton, who will both be in recovery mode from the rear of the field. The two drivers know exactly what it takes to master the wet conditions and celebrate victory in Brazil, so we could see another special day tomorrow. 
 We'll be back up and running from 16:00 GMT on Sunday for race build up. 
 Lights out is at 17:00. 
 See you tomorrow! 
 19 3 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Lawson to start P3 in Brazil published at 20:54 GMT 20:54 GMT 
 Right, Lando Norris is on pole, Kimi Antonelli will take team-mate George Russell's place and start alongside the McLaren driver on the front row and Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson is now promoted to third on the grid from his fifth place in qualifying. 
 Nico Hulkenberg will take his spot in P4 from P6, Isack Hadjar is now fifth, while Oliver Bearman gains two places from eighth to Hulkenberg's sixth. 
 Fernando Alonso and Alex Albon are also lifted with Charles Leclerc's penalty to P8 and P9 respectively, and (I think) Oscar Piastri now gets a spot in the points in 10th after he was knocked out in Q2. 
 Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen will be starting at the back of the grid with their separate grid penalties.
 35 7 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'I didn't know what was coming' - Antonelli published at 20:50 GMT 20:50 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli, who qualified in third but will start the race in second spot after team-mate George Russell takes a five-place grid penalty: "It was very tricky. To be fair, I didn't really know what to expect. Obviously, never drove here in the wet, so I didn't know what was coming.
 "I struggled a little bit on the inters, to be fair, and did a big mistake, almost went off in Turn Five. But it still was enough for P3, so happy with that and now we'll focus on tomorrow. 
 On starting on the front row: "First of all, let's see the weather, how it is going to be, but overall, we'll try to be ready for anything. If it's going to be wet, obviously a lot more knowledge ahead of tomorrow. But let's see, because the weather has been very unpredictable. We will try to be ready for anything.
 "And thank you to all the fans for staying up with us tonight."
 25 2 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'We should've finished the lap' - Russell published at 20:46 GMT 20:46 GMT 
 Mercedes' George Russell, who qualified P2 but will start P7 with a five-place grid penalty: "Obviously congrats to Lando [Norris] but that was definitely the pole lap. Misjudgment on our side, we need to understand what happened. And yeah, the rain was coming and we should've just finished the lap." 
 On what he can do in tomorrow's race: "It depends on the weather. It's the first time in a while I've felt confident in the car; I felt more confident in the wet than I do in the dry, so I don't really understand why that was. 
 "I felt more like myself and could fight for pole every single lap. But unfortunately, when it mattered, we couldn't execute." 
 25 7 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'I think I figured it out pretty quick' - Norris published at 20:41 GMT 20:41 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images McLaren's Lando Norris who will start the race in pole position: "It has been a long day. It has been a great qualifying, to be on pole again here, two years in a row. Different conditions to last year but I am very happy, it's not easy conditions out there, especially when you know it is going to rain a lot more. It was about getting two laps in, in the beginning and not make a mistake, that is exactly what we did so it has been a very good day.
 "This was my first time driving the car in the wet so I think I figured it out pretty quick. Full wet, inters, all different tyres, it was very windy as well the last couple of laps so it is certainly a good day for learning for me and good to take into tomorrow. These guys [Mercedes] are also very quick. Today is just about getting on pole, doesn't matter how you do it so very pleased with that."
 54 13 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 20:37 GMT 20:37 GMT 
 Sorry, Charles. I've completely forgotten about your 10-place grid penalty. So shuffle everyone in the top 10 around, as Ferrari's Leclerc will be starting outside the points in P14. 
 It's been a long qualifying session. 
 78 21 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 20:30 GMT 20:30 GMT 
 So with the George Russell penalty applied, Kimi Antonelli moves up to the front row in P2 and Charles Leclerc will share the second row with Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson in third and fourth. 
 Audi's Nico Hulkenberg will start fifth in Sao Paulo, with Isack Hadjar bumped up to sixth on the grid. 
 Then it's Russell with his penalty, followed by Oliver Bearman, Fernando Alonso and the Williams Alex Albon. 
 58 74 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing

 127 44 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Norris on pole in Sao Paulo published at 20:25 GMT 20:25 GMT 
 We can only see his eyes, but they don't lie - George Russell is very unhappy. 
 The rain is falling heavily and most drivers are getting out of the car, so it looks like we're finally done at Interlagos. 
 Lando Norris will start on pole position tomorrow alongside the man who has replaced him as world champion, Kimi Antonelli. 
 204 30 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 20:24 GMT 20:24 GMT 
 Sam Bird 
Former Formula E driver on 5 Sports Extra 
 There is no point of running if it is like this, if the track is getting slower and slower.
 George Russell looks absolutely raging at the moment in the cockpit of the Mercedes.
 94 38 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 20:23 GMT 20:23 GMT 
 George Russell is fuming on the Mercedes team radio. He first came up against his best mate Alex Albon and told him to get out of the way, and now he says his team told him to back off. He's P2 at the moment, which will be P7 when his penalty is applied, but he says he doesn't want second, he wants P1. 
 127 61 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 20:21 GMT 20:21 GMT 
 Sam Bird 
Former Formula E driver on 5 Sports Extra 
 He has come alive a bit, Lando Norris, hasn't he? In the latter stages of this qualifying session. George Russell vs Lando Norris seems to be the first right now. 
 109 25 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Norris beats Russell published at 20:20 GMT 20:20 GMT 
 The fight was predicted to be between Lando Norris and George Russell, and the McLaren driver puts in an improved lap time to jump back onto provisional pole. 
 Russell has a five-place drop, so the likes of Kimi Antonelli and Charles Leclerc will move up the order. 
 The rain is coming down heavy now with seven minutes remaining. 
 121 32 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Russell on provisional pole published at 20:19 GMT 20:19 GMT 
 Lando Norris goes on to provisional pole position but George Russell crosses the line to leapfrog the McLaren and pushes him down into second. 
 Liam Lawson is third on the grid as it stands, with world champion Kimi Antonelli in fourth. 
 Fernando Alonso goes again but he stays P8. 
 93 37 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 20:18 GMT 20:18 GMT 
 So who is going to get a banker lap in and possibly sneak a surprise pole position before the rain arrives? Fernando Alonso is out on track, his last pole being way back in 2012 when he was still at Ferrari. 
 The Spaniard clocks a 1:30.311, which isn't good enough for the top, unfortunately. 
 42 32 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 20:16 GMT 20:16 GMT 
 Sam Bird 
Former Formula E driver on 5 Sports Extra 
 At the moment I would say George Russell is my favourite [for pole position]. But Liam Lawson is looking strong, Fernando Alonso is looking strong. Honestly you could pick five or six people out there that could get pole position.
 87 23 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Go! Go! Go! published at 20:15 GMT 20:15 GMT 
 Here we go then. 
 Bono is back on the radio to world champion Kimi Antonelli to say the rain is going to be intense. 
 Image source, Reuters 
 64 19 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 20:14 GMT 20:14 GMT 
 The session is going to start shortly, but Kimi Antonelli is being told by Mercedes he may only get one lap in before it lashes down. 
 61 14 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 20:12 GMT 20:12 GMT 
 The dark clouds are gathering again at Interlagos, and this could be a lot of rain that's about to be dumped on the track. 
 Q3 is delayed anyway so that the marshals can repair the barriers following Rafa Camara's crash at Turn 12, but cars are starting to line up in the pit lane, again on intermediate tyres.
